anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: It is to your advantage that I go away.
Unless the grain of wheat dies, it remains alone; if it dies, it bears much fruit.
Behold I and the children God has given me.

pass_a_gloss: And of those who heard and were in some way grieved, he said: It profits you that I go away; for the grain of wheat unless it dies remains alone, but if it dies it bears much fruit, which he confesses with: Behold I and the children whom God has given me.
pass_b_english: And of those who heard and were in a way grieved, he said: "It is to your advantage that I go away; for unless the grain of wheat dies, it remains alone, but if it dies, it bears much fruit," which he confesses with: "Behold I and the children whom God has given me."
source_text: Καὶ τῶν δὲ ἀκουσάντων καὶ τρόπῳ τινὶ λυπηθέντων, εἶπεν· "Συμφέρει ὑμῖν ἵνα ἐγὼ ἀπελθῶ· ὁ γὰρ κόκκος τοῦ σίτου ἐὰν μὴ ἀποθάνῃ, μόνος μένει, ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ, πολὺν καρπὸν φέρει", ὅπερ ὁμολογεῖ <τῷ>· "Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ καὶ τὰ παιδία ἅ μοι ἔδωκεν ὁ θ(εό)ς.
